paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is holy, and He wants His people to treat what belongs to Him that way. He tells the priests to treat the sacred offerings with respect "so that they do not profane My holy name" (Leviticus 22:2). And look at how it closes: "I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites" (Leviticus 22:32). Everything in this chapter, the eating rules and the offering rules, points back to that one thing.

Now hear me, because this part matters: God sets a high bar for what goes on His altar, and He doesn't want leftovers, friend. A burnt offering had to be an unblemished male, and anything with a defect would not be accepted (Leviticus 22:19-20), though an ox or sheep with a deformed or stunted limb could be a freewill offering, but not for a vow (Leviticus 22:23). I know a little something about wanting the best, because nobody has ever served a cookie to the Marriage Supper out of the crumb pile. But notice who does the real work: God says of the priests, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them" (Leviticus 22:9).

So what does that mean for you, baker? God told Israel to keep His commandments and practice them (Leviticus 22:31). He is the LORD "who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God" (Leviticus 22:33), and that rescue was spoken to Israel. What carries over to you is that this same God is holy and worth your best, so give it with respect.
